label: Late original phase / <DEL> step, boosted by k/n/j at the sequence start or x/h/i/d just input
explanation: Fires only in the later part of the original-input phase (t >= 4, peaking at orig_idx 5-7) and on the <DEL> step (30% of mass). It is almost silent at t <= 2 and in the copy phase (0.4% of mass, nearly all at the first copy step). The timing envelope (phase <= 1 & t >= 4) covers 98% of activations but has only 29% precision. Which sequences fire depends on content: having k, n or j as the first (or second) original token roughly triples the rate (top examples nearly all start with k/n/j), and a previous input of x, h, i or d also raises it. Activation magnitude ramps up over consecutive late original steps and peaks around t = 5-7 or at <DEL>. First occurrences of a token fire more often than repeats. The content dependence is graded and spread across many tokens, so the disjunctive predicate reaches only about 0.6 F1.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: n, k, j, p, r, u; least: m, d, 0, x) and the previous input (most: x, h, i, d, <DEL>, 3; least: q, p, k, -); timing cues that raise it most: t=6, t=5, t=7.
